## Full current page content [food-safety]

# Food Safety

Preventing foodborne illness through proper handling, storage, and preparation.

## Temperature Danger Zone

Bacteria multiply rapidly between 4 °C and 60 °C. Perishable food should not remain in this range for more than two hours (one hour above 32 °C ambient).


> [!warning] Contradiction — CD-001 · open
> **A** — 2026-08-12 · `src/seed-corpus` — Bacteria multiply rapidly between 4 °C and 60 °C.
> **B** — 2026-08-12 · `src/food-safety-update` — Bacteria multiply rapidly in food held at temperatures between 5 °C and 63 °C.
> The two claims assert different numeric boundaries for the same danger zone, and the source only gestures at 'refined understanding' without stating that a specific threshold was changed from one value to another.

> [!warning] Contradiction — CD-002 · open
> **A** — 2026-08-12 · `src/seed-corpus` — Perishable food should not remain in the temperature range of 4 °C to 60 °C for more than two hours.
> **B** — 2026-08-12 · `src/food-safety-update` — Food held in the temperature range of 5 °C to 63 °C for more than two hours should be discarded.
> The holding time agrees but the temperature range defining it conflicts, and no explicit change event is stated in the source.
## Cross-Contamination

Raw meat, poultry, and seafood must be stored below ready-to-eat foods. Separate cutting boards and utensils prevent transfer of pathogens like Salmonella and Campylobacter.


Some 2024 guidance defines the danger zone slightly more widely, as 5 °C to 63 °C, and advises discarding food held in that range for more than two hours. The two figures reflect different regulatory conventions rather than a change in the underlying microbiology; the more conservative bound in each direction is the safer working assumption.

*(Source: examples/food-safety-update.md, ingested 2026-08-12)*

Refrigerators should hold below 5 °C at all times, not merely on average — door openings, overpacking, and warm items placed inside can push internal temperatures above the threshold. A fridge thermometer is more reliable than the appliance's own dial setting.

*(Source: examples/food-safety-update.md, ingested 2026-08-12)*

Poultry — including chicken, turkey, and duck — should reach an internal temperature of 74 °C before serving.

This figure was explicitly revised in 2024 from the earlier recommendation of 82 °C, following updated research on pathogen destruction. The revision is a stated change event, not a conflict of conventions: the 82 °C figure is superseded rather than merely an alternative bound.

Internal temperature should be measured at the thickest part of the meat, away from bone.

*(Source: examples/poultry-temperature-revision.md, ingested 2026-08-12)*

# Sauerkraut Fermentation

Basic sauerkraut fermentation takes 14 days at room temperature. The cabbage should be submerged in its own brine throughout the process to prevent mould growth.
